'''Keisha Cook''' is an assistant professor for the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences at [[Clemson University]].

== Biography ==
Cook was born in the suburbs just outside Marietta, Georgia.<ref>{{Cite web |title={{!}} Keisha Cook |url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/keisha-cook/ |access-date=2023-04-10 |language=en-US}}</ref> After receiving her Bachelor of Science from the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham|University of Alabama]] for applied mathematics she then began work on her Masters of Arts, which she completed in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spring 2014 Graduates Announced at UA – Page 5 – University of Alabama News {{!}} The University of Alabama |date=2 May 2014 |url=https://news.ua.edu/2014/05/spring-2014-graduates-announced-at-ua/5/ |access-date=2023-04-10 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Staff Writer |title=University of Alabama winter commencement 2016: Full list of graduates |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/news/education/campus/2016/12/11/university-of-alabama-winter-commencement-2016-full-list-of-graduates/24282127007/ |access-date=2023-04-10 |website=The Tuscaloosa News |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Education and research ==
Cook received her Ph.D. in 2019 for Applied Mathematics and Computational Biology at the University of Alabama under the supervision of [[Rodger B. Sidje]]; her thesis concerned [[Parallel computing|parallel]] [[stochastic simulation]] of biochemical reaction systems.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Keisha Cook – The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=262661 |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> She held a postdoctoral position jointly at [[Tulane University]] and the Southeast Center for Mathematics and Biology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Featured Graduate Students and Postdoctoral Fellows {{!}} Office Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies |url=https://ogps.tulane.edu/featured-graduate-students-and-postdoctoral-fellows |access-date=2024-04-05 |website=ogps.tulane.edu}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2021 Cook was a part of a team that received a $3,799 grant to fund their Math for All conference.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NSF Award Search: Award # 2113829 – Conference: Math For All in New Orleans |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2113829&HistoricalAwards=false |access-date=2023-04-10 |website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref> Later the same year a $49,951 for the annual Math for All conference was granted to the same team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NSF Award Search: Award # 2138357 – Conference: Math for All |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2138357&HistoricalAwards=false |access-date=2023-04-10 |website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref> In 2022 Dr. Cook received a grant from the Clemson University research fellows for $150,000.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Clemson Research Fellows |url=https://www.clemson.edu/research/division-of-research/resources/r-init-sub-pages/research-fellows.html |access-date=2023-04-10 |website=Clemson Research Fellows |language=en-US}}</ref>

Cook has been invited to many talks including a two part talk series at the University of Alabama in 2020, and a collaborative [[Association for Women in Mathematics|AWM]] and [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] meeting in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AWM Talk Series – Dr. Keisha Cook (Tulane University) – Mathematics |url=https://math.ua.edu/event/awm-talk-series-dr-keisha-cook-tulane-university/ |access-date=2023-04-10 |website=math.ua.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=AWM Research Symposium |url=https://awm-math.org/meetings/awm-research-symposium/ |access-date=2023-04-11 |website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2022 Cook was awarded a [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] [[SIAM]] Early Career Fellowship.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MGB-SIAM Early Career Fellowship |url=https://www.siam.org/students-education/programs-initiatives/mgb-siam-early-career-fellowship |access-date=2023-04-12 |website=www.siam.org}}</ref>

In 2024, Cook was named a Gilliam Advisor to Gilliam Fellow Jakini Kauba. They were one of 50 mentor/student pairs taking part in a prestigious program recognizing outstanding advisor/graduate student partnerships organized by the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bunch |first1=Jill E. |title=Ph.D. student lands prestigious Gilliam Fellowship |url=https://news.clemson.edu/ph-d-student-lands-prestigious-gilliam-fellowship/ |website=Clemson News |date=17 July 2024 |access-date=15 October 2024}}</ref>
